accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE National Curriculum in England, science Year 4 Sound ('recognise that sounds get fainter as the distance from the sound source increases') and its non-statutory guidance on using data loggers/sound meters. The physics matches the inverse square law for a small source in open air: intensity falls as 1/r², which is 20·log10(2) ≈ 6.02 dB per doubling (Physics Classroom / HyperPhysics 'Inverse square law, sound'). The lab computes every reading as 80 − 20·log10(d) and rounds: 80, 74, 70, 68, 66, 64, 63, 62 dB at 1–8 m and 56 dB at 16 m; soft hit 70 dB → 58 dB at 4 m, 52 dB at 8 m; hard hit 82 dB → 58 dB at 16 m. The adult text notes air absorption and that walls, echoes and wind change real readings, and that sound's speed does not change. The ripple-ring picture is a flat model and is described only as 'spread over a bigger area', not as an exact count.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the misconceptions documented in the ASE/Science Learning Hub and Driver et al. 'Making Sense of Secondary Science' sound chapter: sound 'gets tired', runs out of energy or slows down (prediction option, challenge tags tired and m8 thunder item), sound stops suddenly at a set distance (prediction 'stays the same, then stops', the 0 dB graph option, the graph feedback 'it does not suddenly stop'), loud sounds do not fade (the hard-hit step, mastery m4, tag nofade), the reading going up or staying flat further away (tags up and flat, graph feedback), and changing two variables in a test (fair-test sort, tags fair and meter).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagfade is about distance and loudness only: a listener dragged along a 1–8 m path beside a drum with a live dB meter and a recorded readings table, a bar chart whose 16 m bar the learner drags to continue the −6 dB-per-doubling pattern, three ripple rings each carrying the same 24 'dots of shake' with fixed ear windows that catch fewer dots on bigger rings, a soft-hit/hard-hit line with a 58 dB playground-noise threshold, and a keep/change/measure sort for a fair test. It differs from flagmedium (sound through solids, liquids, gases), flagvib (vibrations), flagloud (making loud and quiet sounds) and flaghear (frequency range); the gate reports under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner gathers the evidence before the text gives the rule: recording four readings shows the number falling with distance; continuing the bar chart forces them to find the 6 dB step and see that the sound fades gradually rather than stopping; tapping the rings shows the same shake spread over a bigger ring so fewer dots reach the ear (the 'why'); the two hits show a louder start is heard further but still fades; and the sort builds the fair-test plan. Each step's summary appears only when the task is done.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'stays the same, then stops' (the meter drops at every step), 62 dB or 0 dB at 16 m (the pattern gives 56), 'the sound gets tired and slows down' (the rings show spreading with no slowing), 'loud sounds do not fade' (the hard hit drops to 58 dB by 16 m), and 'change the distance and how hard you hit' (the sort says keep the hit the same). The task message echoes the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each, mapped to distinct messages: louder and same (moving away makes the same sound fainter), tired and light (sound does not tire or turn into light; its shake spreads out), up and flat (the reading must fall: 70, 64, 58), nofade and sooner (loud sounds fade too; a louder start is heard further, not less far), fair and meter (he changed two things; the meter is fine) and near (the nearer, the louder). In-lab wrong moves also name the slip, e.g. 'At 8 m it reads 52 dB, under the 58 dB playground noise: too faint to hear.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits (kid FK under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid text uses short sentences and a ripple-on-a-pond image, and introduces the Year 4 words exactly: source, vibrate, fainter, louder, sound meter, fair test. Canvas prompts are one line ('Tap each ring to see how much shake reaches the ear.').

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each lab step has one job (observe, pattern, explain, compare sources, plan a test) and every feedback line carries a reading, a distance or a rule. Item explanations give the reason (two doublings take off 12 dB; he changed two things) rather than repeating the question.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark on every step after Show me. First-pass fixes: the dB value sat on the dark meter bar and was moved beside it; ring counts overlapped the arcs and now sit in a list at the top left; the playground-noise note was clipped and now wraps; the fair-test card names spilled out of the narrow boxes and now appear as full-width 'Keep the same: …' lines; the challenge canvas shows the finished bar chart instead of crowded labels. All canvas actions are repeated by full-size buttons.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: '◀ Closer', 'Further ▶', 'Record reading', 'Bar down'/'Bar up'/'Check', 'Ring 1–3', one button per distance for the hits, and the three sort boxes. After each move the canvas aria-label states the situation in words ('Listener 4 metres from the drum. Meter: 68 decibels. 2 of 4 readings recorded.'). Challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.
